question: What minimum vertical clearance is required for overhead signs over the pavement and shoulders?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Overhead signs must provide a minimum vertical clearance of 17 feet, measured to the sign, light fixture, or sign bridge, over the entire width of the pavement and shoulders. The only exception is where the mounting structure or other nearby structures along the roadway have a lesser vertical clearance, in which case reduced clearances are permitted under limited conditions. Standards (mandatory): - Per Section 2A.15 (shown on the attached page): "Overhead signs shall provide a vertical clearance of not less than 17 feet to the sign, light fixture, or sign bridge over the entire width of the pavement and shoulders, except where the structure on which the overhead signs are to be mounted or other structures along the roadway near the sign structure have a lesser vertical clearance." - Also from the same page: "Signs that are post-mounted on a median barrier that overhang any portion of the traveled way shall be mounted with a vertical clearance that complies with that of overhead signs." - Related lateral requirement: "For overhead sign supports, the minimum lateral offset from the edge of the shoulder (or if no shoulder exists, from the edge of the pavement) to the near edge of overhead sign supports (cantilever or sign bridges) shall be 6 feet. Overhead sign supports shall have a barrier or crash cushion to shield them if they are within the clear zone." Options (permitted): - If the vertical clearance of other structures along the roadway near the sign structure is less than 16 feet, the vertical clearance to an overhead sign structure or support may be as low as 1 foot higher than the vertical clearance of the other structures, in order to improve visibility of the overhead signs (shown on the attached page); in special cases the clearance may be reduced because of substandard dimensions in tunnels and other major structures such as double-deck bridges. - Where lateral clearance is limited, Preferential Lane regulatory signs post-mounted on a median barrier (72 inches or less in width) may be mounted higher, such that the vertical clearance to the bottom of the sign, light fixture, or structural support, whichever is lowest, is not less than 17 feet above any portion of the pavement and shoulders. - The same 17-foot minimum applies when warning signs on median barriers for preferential lanes are mounted higher due to limited lateral clearance. - Preferential Lane guide signs 72 inches or less in width may likewise be mounted higher, maintaining not less than 17 feet of vertical clearance above any portion of the pavement and shoulders. Visual evidence: [Image 1] Figure 2A-2, panel H "Overhead sign," illustrates the 17 ft MIN vertical clearance from the roadway to the bottom of an overhead sign, along with the 6 ft MIN lateral offset for the support. [Image 2] contains the Section 2A.15 Standard text requiring not less than 17 feet of vertical clearance over the entire width of the pavement and shoulders, plus the Options for reduced clearance near lower structures. [Image 5] (Section 2E.19/2E.20) notes that vertical clearance of overhead signs is discussed in Section 2A.15 and establishes the 6-foot lateral offset for overhead sign supports on freeways and expressways. [Image 3] and [Image 4] show Figure 2D-10 examples of overhead signs at an intersection but do not add vertical clearance dimensions. Citations: - Page 100 - Figure 2A-2 (p.51) - Section 2A.16 Standard §1 (p.59) - Section 2G.03 Option §14 (p.411) - Section 2G.08 Option §4 (p.419) - Section 2G.10 Option §18 (p.422) - Page 344
gold_answer: At least 17 feet, except where nearby structures or special constrained structures qualify for the specific exceptions in Section 2A.15.
